architectureDecisions: D1 — createExharnessMcpVerifyServer({ worktreeRoot, verifiers, attemptIndex, candidateSha }) returns { start({ stdin, stdout }), stop(), tools }. tools are frozen { exharness_verify, exharness_status }. Constructing with an extra promote/accept/merge tool throws.

D2 — Wire protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0 newline-delimited stdio. Methods: initialize -> protocol version 2026-07-28 capabilities tools; tools/list -> the two tools; tools/call name=exharness_verify -> run declared createLocalCommandVerifier set at worktree HEAD and return { ok, results: [{ name, status, reason }] }; tools/call name=exharness_status -> { attemptIndex, candidateSha, lastVerification }. Unknown names return JSON-RPC error.

D3 — Zero runtime dependency: implement the tiny stdio loop in-package. Official MCP TypeScript SDK (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk, 13.5k stars, MIT) is an eligibility reference and a later optional adapter, not a runtime import in this task. Tests use an in-repo fake client.

D4 — Opt-in wiring: runSupervisedTask({ mcpVerify: false|undefined }) never calls createExharnessMcpVerifyServer. When true, the server is started for the worktree and stopped in finally; adapters are not given a config-file path. READY research gap: how Codex/Kiro discover the server without writing user config (stdio child vs env EXHARNESS_MCP_FD). Pin one before READY; default tests use a fake client on the server's stdio, not a live Codex mcp add.
D5 — exharness_verify never mutates lineage or calls PROMOTE. A test that the fake agent calls verify then claims success still requires outer verifier PASS to ACCEPTED.
D6 — Evidence basis: productization probe mcpFacts all false except oracleStateMcp; BB-097 CLI probe Codex/Kiro mcp add/list true; BB-097 outOfScope deferred in-tool MCP.
D7 — Living: docs/living/system/agent-tools/state.md and docs/living/system/agent-tools/mcp.md stating MCP is a verification query transport.
